prompt: What has happened to a message when produce() returns?

choices.text: It is stored on the broker, in its partition
choices.why: That is only known from the delivery report, later.

choices.text: It has been read by at least one consumer
choices.why: Producing knows nothing of consumers.

choices.text: It is in the client's buffer, waiting to join a batch
choices.why: Right. A thread in the client sends it later.

choices.text: It has been written to the topic's active segment on the client's own disk
choices.why: Segments live on brokers; the client keeps messages in memory.

prompt: Two hundred sales at two hundred a second went in 197 batches with linger.ms=0 and in 11 with linger.ms=100. What did the second setting trade?

choices.text: Up to 100 ms more wait per message, for far fewer requests
choices.why: Right. About eighteen messages shared each trip.

choices.text: Safety for speed: messages in a lingering batch are lost if the broker restarts
choices.why: A waiting batch is still retried until message.timeout.ms; linger is about latency.

choices.text: Order: lingering batches arrive in a different order
choices.why: Batches of one partition keep their order.

choices.text: Disk space on the broker for memory on the client
choices.why: The same 200 messages are stored either way.

prompt: With the cluster stopped, producer.py printed failed: 5 x Local: Message timed out. What does Local mean?

choices.text: The broker refused the messages because the topic was not ready yet
choices.why: There was no broker to refuse anything.

choices.text: The client raised it, having given up
choices.why: Right. After message.timeout.ms, five seconds here.

choices.text: The messages were written to a local file instead
choices.why: Nothing writes them anywhere; the program would have to.

choices.text: The topic exists only on the local machine
choices.why: It is about who raised the error, not where the topic is.

prompt: A till program calls produce() for each sale and never calls poll() or flush(), and never sets a delivery callback. What does it not know?

choices.text: Which partition each sale should go to
choices.why: The partitioner decides that inside produce, report or not.

choices.text: The offsets of the consumer groups that will read
choices.why: No producer knows that, and none needs to.

choices.text: Whether any sale was stored, or was dropped when the program exited
choices.why: Right. Without a report or a flush, a failure is silent.

choices.text: Its own client id
choices.why: That is configuration, known from the start.

prompt: How does a Kafka consumer get messages?

choices.text: The broker pushes each message to it as soon as it is written
choices.why: Kafka is pull-based; nothing arrives unless the consumer asks.

choices.text: It calls poll() in a loop and gets the next one each time
choices.why: Right. And group membership happens inside those calls.

choices.text: It reads the segment files from the broker's disk
choices.why: It asks the broker over the network; it never opens the files.

choices.text: The producer sends a copy to each consumer
choices.why: Producers do not know who consumes.

prompt: c1 printed partition 2's sales first, although oli-000001 had been produced first. Why is that not a bug?

choices.text: Kafka keeps order only within a partition, and oli-000001 is in partition 0
choices.why: Right. Each partition came out in offset order.

choices.text: Recife's sales have priority
choices.why: Kafka has no priorities between keys.

choices.text: The consumer sorts by key
choices.why: Nothing sorts; partitions are fetched side by side.

choices.text: auto.offset.reset=earliest reads the newest partition first
choices.why: It says where a new group starts in each partition, not which partition comes first.

prompt: A new group subscribes to a topic that already holds a week of sales, with auto.offset.reset left at its default. What does it read first?

choices.text: The oldest sale still stored
choices.why: That is earliest; the default is latest.

choices.text: A sale produced after it joined
choices.why: Right. latest starts at the end of each partition.

choices.text: The sales the previous group left unread
choices.why: Groups do not share positions.

choices.text: Nothing: it fails until a position is set
choices.why: It fails only with auto.offset.reset=none.

prompt: A partition has LOG-END-OFFSET 120 and the group's CURRENT-OFFSET is 95. What is the LAG?
Four copies of a program run with the same group.id on a topic of four partitions. Who reads partition 2?

choices.text: All four copies, each a share of its messages
choices.why: A partition is never split between members.

choices.text: Exactly one of the copies
choices.why: Right. One reader per partition within a group.

choices.text: Whichever copy calls poll first for each message
choices.why: Assignment is per partition, decided at the rebalance.

choices.text: Nobody until a copy asks for it by number
choices.why: subscribe hands partitions out; nobody asks by number.

prompt: The loyalty scheme starts a new consumer group on sales while the stock group is running. What happens to the stock group?

choices.text: It loses half of its partitions to the new group
choices.why: Partitions are shared within a group, not between groups.

choices.text: It rebalances, because the topic has a new reader
choices.why: A rebalance is about one group's membership; other groups do not count.

choices.text: Its offsets are reset to the new group's
choices.why: Each group keeps its own offsets.

choices.text: Nothing: it keeps its partitions and offsets
choices.why: Right. Every group reads every message at its own place.

prompt: In group shelf, b held partition 1 when ten new sales arrived. Who else in shelf read partition 1's new sales?

choices.text: a, which had read the whole topic before
choices.why: a then held partition 2 only.

choices.text: Nobody
choices.why: Right. Within a group each message is read by one member.

choices.text: d, as a standby copy
choices.why: A standby holds nothing and reads nothing.

choices.text: c, which shares partitions 0 and 1 with b
choices.why: Partitions are not shared inside a group; c had partition 0.

prompt: When does a consumer group rebalance?

choices.text: Every five seconds, to spread the load
choices.why: Five seconds is the auto commit interval, a different thing.

choices.text: Whenever a producer writes to a new partition
choices.why: Producers do not trigger rebalances.

choices.text: Only when an administrator asks
choices.why: It happens by itself whenever the membership changes.

choices.text: When a member joins or leaves
choices.why: Right. Including a crash or a member too slow to poll.

prompt: With the eager range strategy, b joined a group in which a held partitions 0, 1 and 2, and a ended with 0 and 1. What happened to partitions 0 and 1 in between?

choices.text: Nothing: they stayed with a and kept being read
choices.why: That is incremental behaviour; eager revokes everything.

choices.text: a gave them back and got them again, and nobody read them meanwhile
choices.why: Right. Every partition stops in an eager rebalance.

choices.text: b read them while a waited
choices.why: b only ever got partition 2.

choices.text: Their offsets went back to 0
choices.why: Committed offsets stay; only the owner changes.

prompt: Match each protocol or strategy with how it rebalances.

pairs.right: every member gives back every partition
members negotiate; only partitions that move stop
the broker computes each member's changes

right_distractors: partitions are assigned once and never move

prompt: To use Kafka 4's new rebalance protocol from the Python client, set group.protocol=___ .
A topic has three partitions and a group runs five copies. How many copies read nothing?

choices.text: None: the five share each partition's messages
choices.why: A partition has one reader in a group.

choices.text: Two
choices.why: Right. Three partitions, three readers.

choices.text: Three
choices.why: Three copies read, one partition each.

choices.text: All five until one of them leaves
choices.why: Three are assigned at once.

prompt: A consumer of a three-partition topic is too slow, and someone proposes handing each message to a pool of eight threads inside it. What has to be added to keep the order lesson 2 relies on?

choices.text: Nothing: the partition already keeps order
choices.why: The partition delivers in order; parallel threads can finish out of order.

choices.text: Eight partitions, one per thread
choices.why: That changes the topic and moves keys; the threads are inside one member.

choices.text: Send each key always to the same thread
choices.why: Right. Then one key's messages are handled one after another.

choices.text: Commit after each thread finishes
choices.why: Commits decide what a crash repeats, not the order of work.

prompt: What does a group's committed offset of 8 on a partition mean?

choices.text: The group has read offset 8
choices.why: It is the next to read; 0 to 7 are done.

choices.text: The partition holds 8 messages
choices.why: That is the log-end offset, a property of the partition.

choices.text: The group will read offset 8 next
choices.why: Right. Everything before it counts as done.

choices.text: Eight members have read the partition
choices.why: Commits are per group, not per member.

prompt: x read all twenty sales and was killed about four seconds after it started, with automatic commits on. What did the group auto have committed?

choices.text: Nothing for any partition
choices.why: Right. The first automatic commit comes after five seconds.

choices.text: 8, 8 and 4, everything it printed
choices.why: That was the manual group, which committed each message.

choices.text: Half of what it read
choices.why: Automatic commits are not proportional; there was none yet.

choices.text: The last offset of each partition, committed on exit
choices.why: kill -9 gives no chance to commit on exit.

prompt: A consumer commits after processing. Put a crash that causes a duplicate in order.
items: poll returns the message at offset 7
the consumer adds the sale to a total
a new member resumes at the committed 7 and adds it again

prompt: Where does Kafka keep a group's committed offsets?

choices.text: In a file in the consumer's working directory
choices.why: That was minilog.py; Kafka keeps them on the brokers.

choices.text: Inside each message, in a header the broker updates as groups read
choices.why: Messages are never edited after they are written.

choices.text: In the controller's metadata log, beside the topics and the nodes
choices.why: The metadata log holds topics and nodes, not group positions.

choices.text: In __consumer_offsets, a compacted topic
choices.why: Right. Fifty partitions, cleanup.policy=compact.

prompt: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --reset-offsets refuses while the group has running members. Why does it make sense?

choices.text: Resetting deletes messages, which running members are reading
choices.why: A reset deletes nothing; the log supplies the messages again.

choices.text: The broker locks the topic while a group reads it
choices.why: Topics are not locked by readers.

choices.text: Only the group's leader member is allowed to change offsets
choices.why: The tool changes them from outside, once nobody is running.

choices.text: Members would commit over the new ones
choices.why: Right. Stop the group, move its place, start it again.

prompt: rewind.py uses assign() instead of subscribe(). What follows?

choices.text: It joins the group rewind and takes partitions from its members
choices.why: An assigned consumer is in no group and causes no rebalance.

choices.text: It reads only partition 0, the first one the broker lists
choices.why: It assigns every partition the broker returned.

choices.text: It reads where it says, in no group
choices.why: Right. A tool for looking, not for sharing work.

choices.text: It commits the new offsets for every group
choices.why: It commits nothing; auto commit is off.

prompt: Group stock had committed 4 on partition 1, and partition 1's log-end offset was 8. It was reset to offset 3 on partition 1. How many messages from partition 1 did c1 then read?
A shop's stock consumer must not count a sale twice, runs as three copies on a topic of three partitions, and a fourth copy is started for safety. Which statement is true?

choices.text: The fourth copy reads a quarter of every partition
choices.why: Partitions are not split; it holds none.

choices.text: The fourth copy is a standby, and committing after processing still risks a duplicate after a crash
choices.why: Right. Membership and commits are separate problems; lesson 8 handles the second.

choices.text: Adding the fourth copy guarantees no sale is counted twice
choices.why: Copies do not change what a crash between work and commit does.

choices.text: With four copies, automatic commits are turned off
choices.why: The number of members has nothing to do with commit settings.
